svg.title: What adopting an open-source AI stack moves and what it leaves with you
svg.desc: Two columns. The left column lists what open source transfers: who runs the software, who maintains the deployment, where conversation and run data sit, and the software licence line item. The right column lists what it does not remove: model API calls, market and news data access, hosting and uptime, upgrades and security response, and judging whether the output is any good. A bottom strip shows the two audited projects answering different jobs: TradingAgents is a research-only multi-agent trading framework, LibreChat is a self-hosted chat interface over providers you bring.
svg.text: Open source changes the operator, not the bill
Read at TradingAgents be952b8e and LibreChat e18606e5

g.text: What adoption really transfers
• Who runs the software: a vendor → your team
• Who maintains the deployment and its config
• Where conversation and run data sit
• The software licence line item itself
Apache-2.0 and MIT are the source notes,
not a statement about your running cost.
What it does not remove
• Model API calls you still pay for or host
• Market, news and data-provider access
• Hosting, uptime and backup
• Upgrades, auth and security response
• Judging whether the output is any good
Both READMEs say this in their own words.
TradingAgents
Multi-agent research framework; the README
states it is not financial or trading advice.
LibreChat
Self-hosted chat platform that unifies the
providers you already bring to it.

svg.text: Different jobs — not substitutes for each other
